findings.source: CrossChainForwarder.sol:429-433 for (uint256 i = 0; i < senders.length; i++) { require(senders[i] != address(0), Errors.INVALID_SENDER); _approvedSenders[senders[i]] = newState; emit SenderUpdated(senders[i], newState); } (and the similar loops at CrossChainReceiver.sol:249, :269, :292, CrossChainForwarder.sol:323, :394)
findings.issue: The loop header is the body's require (senders[i] != address(0), or the flag of a similar check: 'while _36', 'while address(_27)'), whose failure leaves the loop to the revert printed after it, while the source condition i < length is printed as 'if s + 1 >= len: stop' at the bottom and its first test peeled before the loop. 'while address(_20)' reads as a loop over a linked list, not over the array.
findings.rule: Choose as the loop header the test whose exit edge reaches the normal continuation, not one whose exit reaches only a revert: 'while C_revert: B; if i + 1 >= N: exit; i = i + 1' is 'while i < N: require C_revert; B; i = i + 1' (same rule as in c00050).

summary: Faithful text in which all 14 source loops are found, but eight of them are rotated around their require check (the while condition is the check whose failure reverts), and error-code strings and struct-array decodings add many compiler loops and dead memory writes.
